content.intro: Money speaks the language every business must learn. From cash to capital, money talks if you listen.
content.core: Three currencies of business: revenue (what you earn), profit (what you keep), and cash (what you can spend). Each tells a different story about company health.
content.cta: Learn the language of money this module.

content.intro: Three financial statements tell the complete story of any business.
content.core: Income Statement (P&L) — profitability over time. Balance Sheet — financial position at a moment. Cash Flow Statement — actual cash movement.
content.cta: Pull your three statements and read them like a story.

content.intro: Gross margin is the heartbeat of your business model.
content.core: Gross Margin = (Revenue − COGS) / Revenue. It reveals whether your core economics work before any overhead.
content.cta: Calculate gross margin by product line.

content.intro: Burn rate measures how fast you're spending what you have.
content.core: Monthly burn = cash out − cash in. Runway = cash on hand / monthly burn.
content.cta: Calculate your runway and stress-test it.

content.intro: The bottom line — net income — is what's left after every cost.
content.core: Net Income = Revenue − COGS − OpEx − Interest − Taxes. It funds growth, dividends, or reinvestment.
content.cta: Reconcile your bottom line to your bank balance.

content.intro: Cash runway is the oxygen tank of every business.
content.core: Runway in months = Cash / Monthly Burn. Below 6 months — raise. Below 3 — emergency mode.

content.title: April Cash Timing
content.intro: Cash is king, but timing is everything.
content.core: Revenue recognition vs. cash receipt; accounts receivable aging; cash conversion cycle.
content.song_tie_in: April represents the quarterly crunch when cash timing makes or breaks operations.
content.cta: Map your own cash conversion cycle using the worksheet.
image_prompts: A clock with dollar bills as hands, showing cash flowing at different speeds
A river with stepping stones labeled "Invoice," "30 days," "60 days," "Payment"
Calendar with April circled, money flowing into and out of a vault
worksheet: List your top 5 revenue sources and average days to payment
Calculate your cash conversion cycle
Identify which receivables are 30/60/90+ days
Create a 13-week cash flow forecast
Reflection: What one change would most improve your cash timing?
content.calculator_inputs: Monthly revenue, avg days to collect, avg days to pay suppliers
content.calculator_outputs: Cash conversion cycle, weekly cash position, gap analysis

content.intro: Strategy is the bridge between where you are and where you want to be.
